correctness.rationale: The involution swapping the first two coordinates on [q]^3 has fixed-vertex orbits A_{a,c} and two-element orbits B_{ab,c}; each B orbit spans an edge in VR_{≤2}. Geometric fixed points have equal barycentric weights on each orbit, identifying the fixed space with a flag orbit complex L_q. All maximal facets classify as q row simplices S_c, q² symbol-column simplices T_{a,c}, and N=q(q−1)C(q,2)=q²(q−1)²/2 attachment triangles U_{a,b,c,d}. For the S/T-only subcomplex Y, deleting B vertices yields links covered by S,T_a,T_b with interval nerve, so each link is contractible; Y≃the clique complex of the q×q rook graph≃K_{q,q}. Each U triangle attaches along a rectangle loop of K_{q,q}; the (q−1)² rectangles based at a fixed row and column kill the free π1. Relative homology gives H2=Z^{N−(q−1)²}=Z^{(q−1)²(q²−2)/2}, no other positive homology. A simply connected 2-dimensional CW model is homotopy equivalent to that many 2-spheres by Hurewicz and Whitehead. Independently checked actual maximal facets q=3:30, q=4:92, and reduced mod2 Betti 2 respectively 14 and 63; no all-q inference from finite checks.
residual_risks: An unindexed generalized equivariant clique-complex theorem could subsume the q-polynomial classification.
